**Comparability note:** All five companies report on a calendar fiscal year (Jan 1 – Dec 31), so the periods line up directly [DOC-1]. One caveat not resolvable from the excerpt: Alaska Air Group's FY2024 includes Hawaiian Holdings from the September 2024 acquisition close, so its revenue growth is partly inorganic and not strictly like-for-like with the other four carriers' organic growth. The figures below are as-reported.

**Revenue growth, FY2023 → FY2024**

| Rank | Airline | FY2023 | FY2024 | Growth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Alaska | $10,426M | $11,735M | +12.6% [DOC-1] |
| 2 | United | $53,717M | $57,063M | +6.2% [DOC-1] |
| 3 | Delta | $58,048M | $61,643M | +6.2% [DOC-1] |
| 4 | Southwest | $26,091M | $27,483M | +5.3% [DOC-1] |
| 5 | American | $52,788M | $54,211M | +2.7% [DOC-1] |

(United 6.23% vs. Delta 6.19% — effectively a tie, separated by ~4 basis points.)

**Operating margin, FY2024 (operating income ÷ revenue)**

| Rank | Airline | Op. income | Revenue | Margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Delta | $5,995M | $61,643M | 9.7% [DOC-1] |
| 2 | United | $5,096M | $57,063M | 8.9% [DOC-1] |
| 3 | Alaska | $570M | $11,735M | 4.9% [DOC-1] |
| 4 | American | $2,614M | $54,211M | 4.8% [DOC-1] |
| 5 | Southwest | $321M | $27,483M | 1.2% [DOC-1] |

**Is the top-ranked airline the same?** No. Alaska leads on revenue growth (+12.6%, aided by the Hawaiian acquisition), while Delta leads on FY2024 operating margin (9.7%); Alaska ranks only third on margin and Delta third on growth.

ANSWER: No — revenue growth ranking: Alaska (+12.6%), United (+6.2%), Delta (+6.2%), Southwest (+5.3%), American (+2.7%); FY2024 operating margin ranking: Delta (9.7%), United (8.9%), Alaska (4.9%), American (4.8%), Southwest (1.2%). Alaska tops growth (partly from the Hawaiian acquisition) while Delta tops margin.
